title: Impact of New Seed Variety Adoption on Farm Income

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Two-Stage Least Squares (Instrumental-Variables).  
Why: Adoption of the new seed variety (`x`) may be endogenous (e.g., higher-ability farmers adopt more and also earn more). Agro-ecological suitability (`z`) predicts adoption but should affect income only through adoption and normal input choices, making it a plausible instrument.  

Key assumptions  
1. Relevance:  Cov(z, x) ≠ 0 – farms in more suitable areas are more likely to adopt.  
2. Exclusion:  z affects income y only through its impact on adoption x, conditional on observed controls.  
3. Independence:  z is as-good-as random with respect to unobserved determinants of income once controls are included.  
4. Monotonicity (for LATE interpretation): Suitability does not decrease the probability of adoption for any farm.  

## 2. R Code
```r
# Required packages
required <- c("AER", "sandwich", "lmtest")
new.packages <- required[!(required %in% installed.packages()[,"Package"])]
if(length(new.packages)) install.packages(new.packages, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
lapply(required, require, character.only = TRUE)

# 1. Read the data
data_path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s79_data.csv"
df <- read.csv(data_path)

# 2. Naïve OLS (possibly biased)
ols_formula <- y ~ x + controls
ols <- lm(ols_formula, data = df)
ols_robust <- coeftest(ols, vcov = vcovHC(ols, type = "HC1"))

cat("Naïve OLS (robust s.e.):\n")
print(ols_robust)

# 3. IV / 2SLS
iv_formula <- y ~ x + controls | z + controls   # x instrumented by z
iv <- ivreg(iv_formula, data = df)

# Robust (HC1) standard errors
iv_robust <- coeftest(iv, vcov = vcovHC(iv, type = "HC1"))

cat("\nIV 2SLS (robust s.e.):\n")
print(iv_robust)

# 4. First-stage diagnostics
first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = df)
first_stage_robust <- coeftest(first_stage, vcov = vcovHC(first_stage, type = "HC1"))
fs_fstat <- waldtest(first_stage, . ~ controls, vcov = vcovHC(first_stage, type = "HC1"))
cat("\nFirst-stage coefficient on z (robust s.e.):\n")
print(first_stage_robust["z",])
cat("\nWeak-instrument robust F-statistic (H0: z has no effect on x):\n")
print(fs_fstat$F[2])

# 5. Simple robustness check: add quadratic control
df$controls_sq <- df$controls^2
iv_formula_rb <- y ~ x + controls + controls_sq | z + controls + controls_sq
iv_rb <- ivreg(iv_formula_rb, data = df)
iv_rb_robust <- coeftest(iv_rb, vcov = vcovHC(iv_rb, type = "HC1"))
cat("\nIV with quadratic control (robust s.e.):\n")
print(iv_rb_robust["x",])

# 6. Clear numerical result
coef_iv <- iv_robust["x","Estimate"]
se_iv  <- iv_robust["x","Std. Error"]
cat(sprintf("\n==== Main estimate: Effect of adoption on income ====\nCoefficient = %.4f, Robust s.e. = %.4f\n", 
            coef_iv, se_iv))
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Positive – adopting the higher-yield seed should raise farm income.  
Magnitude: With a standardized income variable (mean≈0, sd≈1), a 1-unit increase in adoption (roughly moving from non-adopter to full adopter) might raise income by ≈0.4–0.8 standard deviations. The IV estimate will likely be larger in magnitude than the OLS estimate because OLS tends to under-estimate returns when better farmers self-select into adoption.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use agroecological suitability as an instrument for new seed variety adoption.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Adopting the new seed variety leads to a significant increase in farm income.
